findings.text: The task folder has no top-level `requirements.md`; the owner's ask for the Mention change ("anything referenceable is clickable, never only a code snippet") is stated only inside `ext/Mention/doc/Mention-notes.md`. A fresh agent cannot check the diff against the owner's words, so add a `requirements.md` (or `plan.md` section) that quotes it and links the prompt.

The diff touches only `ext/Mention/`, yet the folder holds three briefs (`reader/`, `roles/`, `routing/`). `roles/` has no report, proposal or `log` line in its folder, and `reader/` is only a design in `plan.md` with no link from `reader/requirements.md` to it, so what landed and what is open can't be read from the folder alone. Add a short `report.md` per brief, or an index in `plan.md`.

`ext/Mention/readme.md` (lines 4 and 21) still says only "a person or an agent role"; it never says that `@mastermind-x`/`task-mastermind-*`-shaped live agent ids now link, nor that a code span holding only a reference is upgraded. `doc/Mention-notes.md` was updated, but `doc/syntax.md` (the syntax rules) does not mention the code-span rule or the agent link, so it is now stale on "code is left alone".

`Mention.js:108` and `upgrade_code` accept any bare `assistant…` word: `AGENT_KIND` has `/^assistant/`, so inline code like `assistant` or `assistants` (and `minion-` prefixes in prose code) turns into a link to `/framework/ai/sessions/assistant/` that opens no agent. Only upgrade a bare (no `@`) code span when it matches a stricter id shape (for example `assistant-<name>`), or require the `@`.
`upgrade_code` (`Mention.js:216`) bypasses `skip()`, so a `code` inside a `textarea`, or any editable surface, would be rewritten too; harmless today, but the walk below it honours `SKIP_TAGS`.

`mention_html` (the string form) does not apply the code-span upgrade, so `mentions(el)` and `mention_html` now differ on `` `@owner` ``; say so in `Mention-notes.md` or it will surprise the next reader.

No test or screenshot covers the new behaviour; `shots/` holds only `framework-1920.png` and `framework-ext-Chat-v2-1920.png`, neither of which shows a code-span mention. A one-line check in the demo page would prove it.

Simpler path: the same effect could be had by dropping `CODE` from `SKIP_TAGS` only for whole-text matches, instead of a second pass over every `code` element, but the current pass is small and clear; leave it unless it shows up in profiles.
